questions.q: Which privileges does reading a table need?

options.t: BROWSE on the catalog and SELECT on the table
SELECT, USE SCHEMA and USE CATALOG

questions.explain: Reading needs SELECT on the table, USE SCHEMA on its schema and USE CATALOG on its catalog.

questions.q: SELECT is granted on a schema. What does it cover?

options.t: Current and future tables and views in the schema
Only the tables that exist at the time of the grant

questions.explain: A privilege on a catalog or schema applies to current and future objects inside it.

questions.q: How do you stop a group reading a table in Unity Catalog SQL?

options.t: `DENY SELECT ON TABLE t TO grp`
options.why: Unity Catalog SQL has no DENY statement.

options.t: Don't grant it, or REVOKE the grant that gives it
Rename the table so the group's queries no longer find it
Set the table's comment to private

questions.explain: There is no DENY statement in Unity Catalog SQL (DENY belongs to legacy Hive metastore table ACLs); access comes only from grants. An ABAC DENY policy (Beta) exists only for MANAGE ACCESS CONTROL.

questions.q: Who does Databricks generally recommend should own tables?

options.why: Ownership by groups survives people leaving.

questions.explain: Databricks generally recommends granting table ownership to groups.

questions.q: What does a user need to add a governed tag to a column?

options.t: APPLY TAG on the object (or ownership), USE SCHEMA, USE CATALOG, and ASSIGN on the governed tag

questions.explain: Adding tags needs ownership or APPLY TAG plus USE SCHEMA and USE CATALOG; a governed tag also needs ASSIGN on it.

questions.q: A tag is set on a catalog. Which objects inherit it for ABAC?

options.t: Schemas and tables beneath it, but not columns
Everything beneath it, columns included, without exception

questions.explain: Tags at one level apply to all objects beneath it, but don't inherit to the column level.

questions.q: What does Unity Catalog lineage capture?

options.t: Only table-level reads, and only within the same workspace
options.why: It goes down to column level, across workspaces on the metastore.

options.t: Column-level lineage for Spark and SQL queries, across workspaces on the metastore
Only lineage that teams declare in YAML

questions.explain: Lineage is captured automatically down to column level for Spark DataFrame and Databricks SQL queries, across all workspaces on the metastore.

questions.q: A partner without Databricks must read three tables. Which way of sharing fits?

options.why: That reads external sources into Databricks.
That needs a Unity Catalog workspace on the recipient's side.
For joint work without seeing each other's data.

questions.explain: Databricks-to-Open sharing reaches users on any platform, with a bearer token or OIDC federation; Databricks-to-Databricks needs a recipient on a Unity Catalog workspace.

questions.q: Which statements about OpenSharing are correct? (Choose two.)

options.t: Notebooks, volumes and models can be shared only Databricks-to-Databricks
Tables with row filters can be shared as they are
options.why: Tables with row filters or column masks can't be shared.

options.t: A recipient must have Unity Catalog to receive shares
options.why: Unity Catalog isn't required, though it helps.

options.t: Sharing within a region incurs egress cost
options.why: Within a region there is no egress cost.

questions.explain: Shares are read-only collections; recipients read them read-only. Notebooks, volumes, models and metric views need Databricks-to-Databricks sharing.

questions.q: An external Delta table is converted to managed. How long can the conversion be rolled back?

options.t: 7 days, with UNDROP TABLE on the managed copy
14 days, with ALTER TABLE ... UNSET MANAGED

questions.explain: ALTER TABLE t SET MANAGED keeps name, permissions and history; roll back within 14 days with UNSET MANAGED.
